passages.text: Then Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.
passages.sermon: Jesus entered Jericho.\r\nJesus was passing through the city.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν διήρχετο τὴν Ἰεριχώ

passages.text: And there was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, who was very wealthy.
passages.sermon:
A man was there.
His name was Zacchaeus.
Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector.
He was very wealthy.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι καλούμενος Ζακχαῖος καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἀρχιτελώνης καὶ αὐτὸς πλούσιος

passages.text: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but could not see over the crowd because he was small in stature.
passages.sermon:
Zacchaeus was a man.
He was a chief tax collector.
He was very wealthy.
Zacchaeus wanted to see Jesus.
He wanted to know who Jesus was.
A large crowd stood in his way.
Zacchaeus was short.
He could not see over the people.
passages.original: καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν τίς ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ὅτι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ μικρὸς ἦν

passages.text: So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him, since Jesus was about to pass that way.
passages.sermon:
Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector.
He was very wealthy.
He wanted to see Jesus.
Zacchaeus could not see over the crowd.
He was short in stature.
Zacchaeus ran ahead of the crowd.
He climbed a sycamore tree.
He wanted to see Jesus.
Jesus was about to pass that way.
passages.original: καὶ προδραμὼν εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν ἀνέβη ἐπὶ συκομορέαν ἵνα ἴδῃ αὐτόν ὅτι ἐκείνης ἤμελλεν διέρχεσθαι

passages.text: When Jesus came to that place, He looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus came to the place where Zacchaeus was.
Jesus looked up.
Jesus saw Zacchaeus in the tree.
Jesus spoke to Zacchaeus.
Jesus said, “Zacchaeus, come down quickly.”
Jesus said, “I must stay at your house today.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὡς ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον ἀναβλέψας ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Ζακχαῖε σπεύσας κατάβηθι σήμερον γὰρ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου δεῖ με μεῖναι

passages.text: So Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed Him joyfully.
passages.sermon:
Zacchaeus was a tax collector.
\r\nJesus called Zacchaeus by name.
\r\nZacchaeus quickly climbed down from the tree.
\r\nZacchaeus welcomed Jesus into his home.
\r\nZacchaeus felt great joy.
passages.original: Καὶ σπεύσας κατέβη καὶ ὑπεδέξατο αὐτὸν χαίρων

passages.text: And all who saw this began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!”
passages.sermon: Many people saw what happened.\r\nThey began to complain.\r\nThey said, “Jesus has gone to stay with a sinful man.”
passages.original: καὶ ἰδόντες πάντες διεγόγγυζον λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ ἁμαρτωλῷ ἀνδρὶ εἰσῆλθεν καταλῦσαι

passages.text: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.”
passages.sermon:
Zacchaeus was a tax collector.
\r\nHe stood up.
\r\nHe spoke to Jesus, who is called Lord.
\r\nZacchaeus said, "Look, Lord."
\r\nHe said, "I give half of my possessions to the poor."
\r\nHe said, "If I have cheated anyone, I will repay that person four times as much."
passages.original: Σταθεὶς δὲ Ζακχαῖος εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Κύριον Ἰδοὺ τὰ ἡμίσιά μου τῶν ὑπαρχόντων Κύριε τοῖς πτωχοῖς δίδωμι καὶ εἴ τινός τι ἐσυκοφάντησα ἀποδίδωμι τετραπλοῦν

passages.text: Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Zacchaeus.\r\nJesus said, “Today, salvation has come to this house.\r\nThis happened because Zacchaeus also is a son of Abraham.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Σήμερον σωτηρία τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ ἐγένετο καθότι καὶ αὐτὸς υἱὸς Ἀβραάμ ἐστιν

passages.text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus came with a purpose.
Jesus came to seek people who are lost.
Jesus came to save people who are lost.
passages.original: ἦλθεν γὰρ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ζητῆσαι καὶ σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός

passages.text: While the people were listening to this, Jesus proceeded to tell them a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was near Jerusalem.
Many people were listening to Him.
The people believed the kingdom of God would appear very soon.
Jesus began to tell them a parable.
passages.original: Ἀκουόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ταῦτα προσθεὶς εἶπεν παραβολὴν διὰ τὸ ἐγγὺς εἶναι Ἰερουσαλὴμ αὐτὸν καὶ δοκεῖν αὐτοὺς ὅτι παραχρῆμα μέλλει ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀναφαίνεσθαι

passages.text: So He said, “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them a parable.
He said, “A man had noble birth.
This man traveled to a far country.
He went there to receive a kingdom for himself.
He planned to return after receiving his kingship.”
passages.original: εἶπεν οὖν Ἄνθρωπός τις εὐγενὴς ἐπορεύθη εἰς χώραν μακρὰν λαβεῖν ἑαυτῷ βασιλείαν καὶ ὑποστρέψαι

passages.text: Beforehand, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. ‘Conduct business with this until I return,’ he said.
passages.sermon:
A man of noble birth called ten of his servants.
He gave the ten servants ten minas.
He spoke to the servants.
He said, “Conduct business with this money until I return.”
passages.original: καλέσας δὲ δέκα δούλους ἑαυτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δέκα μνᾶς καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Πραγματεύσασθε ἐν ᾧ ἔρχομαι

passages.text: But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We do not want this man to rule over us.’
passages.sermon:
A man of noble birth went to a distant country to become king and then return.
He had subjects in his own country.
These subjects hated him.
They sent a delegation after him.
The delegation gave a message.
They said, “We do not want this man to rule over us.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ πολῖται αὐτοῦ ἐμίσουν αὐτόν καὶ ἀπέστειλαν πρεσβείαν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Οὐ θέλομεν τοῦτον βασιλεῦσαι ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς

passages.text: When he returned from procuring his kingship, he summoned the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what each one had earned.
passages.sermon:
A man went away to receive a kingdom.
He returned after he became king.
He had given money to some of his servants before he left.
He called for these servants to come to him.
He wanted to know what each servant had gained with the money.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐπανελθεῖν αὐτὸν λαβόντα τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ εἶπεν φωνηθῆναι αὐτῷ τοὺς δούλους τούτους οἷς δεδώκει τὸ ἀργύριον ἵνα γνοῖ τίς τί διεπραγματεύσαντο

passages.text: The first servant came forward and said, ‘Master, your mina has produced ten more minas.’
passages.sermon:
A man became king, even though his subjects hated him.
He had given money to his servants before he left.
He returned after receiving his kingdom.
He called his servants to him.
He wanted to know what each servant had gained with the money.
The first servant came forward.
He spoke to the king.
He said, “Master, your mina has produced ten more minas.”
passages.original: Παρεγένετο δὲ ὁ πρῶτος λέγων Κύριε ἡ μνᾶ σου δέκα προσηργάσατο μνᾶς

passages.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to the servant.
The master said, "Well done, good servant."
The master called the servant good.
The master said the servant was faithful in a very small matter.
The master gave the servant authority over ten cities.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Εὖγε ἀγαθὲ δοῦλε ὅτι ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ πιστὸς ἐγένου ἴσθι ἐξουσίαν ἔχων ἐπάνω δέκα πόλεων

passages.text: The second servant came and said, ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’
passages.sermon:
The second servant came.
He spoke to his master.
He said, "Master, your mina has made five minas."
The servant reported the result to his master.
The servant increased the master's money by five times.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ δεύτερος λέγων Ἡ μνᾶ σου κύριε ἐποίησεν πέντε μνᾶς

passages.text: And to this one he said, ‘You shall have authority over five cities.’
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to the second servant.
He said, "You will have authority over five cities."
The master gave this reward because the servant increased his master's money by five times.
The master trusted the servant with greater responsibility.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ τούτῳ Καὶ σὺ ἐπάνω γίνου πέντε πόλεων

passages.text: Then another servant came and said, ‘Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth.
passages.sermon:
Another servant came.
He spoke to his master.
He said, “Master, here is your mina.
I kept it safe.
I wrapped it in a piece of cloth.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἦλθεν λέγων Κύριε ἰδοὺ ἡ μνᾶ σου ἣν εἶχον ἀποκειμένην ἐν σουδαρίῳ

passages.text: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You withdraw what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.’
passages.sermon:
The servant spoke to his master.
The servant said he felt afraid of his master.
The servant believed his master was a harsh man.
The master took what he did not deposit.
The master reaped what he did not sow.
passages.original: ἐφοβούμην γάρ σε ὅτι ἄνθρωπος αὐστηρὸς εἶ αἴρεις ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκας καὶ θερίζεις ὃ οὐκ ἔσπειρας

passages.text: His master replied, ‘You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words. So you knew that I am a harsh man, withdrawing what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to the servant.
The master called him a wicked servant.
The master said, "I will judge you by your own words."
The master asked, "You knew that I am a harsh man?"
The master said, "I take what I did not put in."
The master said, "I gather what I did not plant."
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ Ἐκ τοῦ στόματός σου κρίνω σε πονηρὲ δοῦλε ᾔδεις ὅτι ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος αὐστηρός εἰμι αἴρων ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκα καὶ θερίζων ὃ οὐκ ἔσπειρα

passages.text: Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?’
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to the servant.
The master had given the servant money.
The master asked a question.
He said, "Why did you not put my money in the bank?"
He said, "If you had done this, I could have collected my money with interest when I returned."
The master expected the servant to act wisely with the money.
The master wanted to receive more than he gave.
passages.original: καὶ διὰ τί οὐκ ἔδωκάς μου τὸ ἀργύριον ἐπὶ τράπεζαν κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν σὺν τόκῳ ἂν αὐτὸ ἔπραξα

passages.text: Then he told those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’
passages.sermon:
A master spoke to the people standing nearby.
He gave them a command.
He said, "Take the mina away from this servant."
He said, "Give the mina to the servant who has ten minas."
The master wanted the servant with ten minas to receive more.
The master took away the mina from the servant who had not used it well.
passages.original: Καὶ τοῖς παρεστῶσιν εἶπεν Ἄρατε ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὴν μνᾶν καὶ δότε τῷ τὰς δέκα μνᾶς ἔχοντι

passages.text: ‘Master,’ they said, ‘he already has ten!’
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to the master.
They said, "Master, he already has ten minas."
The master had just ordered them to give the mina to the man with ten minas.
The people noticed that this man already possessed ten minas.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Κύριε ἔχει δέκα μνᾶς

passages.text: He replied, ‘I tell you that everyone who has will be given more; but the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, “I tell you this truth.
Everyone who has something will receive more.
Anyone who does not have will lose even what he has.”
passages.original: Λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι παντὶ τῷ ἔχοντι δοθήσεται ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται

passages.text: And these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them, bring them here and slay them in front of me.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about his enemies.
These people did not want Jesus to rule over them.
Jesus said, “Bring these enemies here.
Kill them in front of me.”
passages.original: πλὴν τοὺς ἐχθρούς μου τούτους τοὺς μὴ θελήσαντάς με βασιλεῦσαι ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ἀγάγετε ὧδε καὶ κατασφάξατε αὐτοὺς ἔμπροσθέν μου

passages.text: After Jesus had said this, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke these words.
He went on ahead of the others.
He traveled toward Jerusalem.
He was going up to the city.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰπὼν ταῦτα ἐπορεύετο ἔμπροσθεν ἀναβαίνων εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: As He approached Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent out two of His disciples, saying, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was traveling to Jerusalem.
He came near Bethphage and Bethany.
These villages are close to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus sent two of His disciples.
He gave them instructions.
He said, "Go into the village ahead of you."
He said, "When you enter it, you will find a colt tied there."
No one has ever sat on this colt.
Untie the colt.
Bring the colt here."
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤγγισεν εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν ἀπέστειλεν δύο τῶν μαθητῶν λέγων Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κατέναντι κώμην ἐν ᾗ εἰσπορευόμενοι εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον ἐφ’ ὃν οὐδεὶς πώποτε ἀνθρώπων ἐκάθισεν καὶ λύσαντες αὐτὸν ἀγάγετε

passages.text: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions.
He said, “If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying the colt?’
Say, ‘The Lord needs it.’”
passages.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμᾶς ἐρωτᾷ Διὰ τί λύετε οὕτως ἐρεῖτε Ὅτι Ὁ Κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει

passages.text: So those who were sent went out and found it just as Jesus had told them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent two of His disciples.
The disciples went out.
They found the colt.
They found it exactly as Jesus had told them.
passages.original: Ἀπελθόντες δὲ οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: As they were untying the colt, its owners asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”
passages.sermon:
Two disciples began to untie a young donkey.
The donkey belonged to some owners.
The owners saw the disciples untying the donkey.
The owners spoke to the disciples.
The owners asked, “Why are you untying the donkey?”
passages.original: λυόντων δὲ αὐτῶν τὸν πῶλον εἶπαν οἱ κύριοι αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτούς Τί λύετε τὸν πῶλον

passages.text: “The Lord needs it,” they answered.
passages.sermon: The disciples spoke to the owners of the colt.\r\nThey said, “The Lord needs it.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν ὅτι Ὁ Κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει

passages.text: Then they led the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it.
passages.sermon: The disciples brought the colt to Jesus.\r\nThey placed their cloaks on the colt.\r\nThey put Jesus on the colt.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐπιρίψαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐπὶ τὸν πῶλον ἐπεβίβασαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: As He rode along, the people spread their cloaks on the road.
passages.sermon:
Jesus rode along the road.
The people saw Jesus.
The people took off their cloaks.
The people spread their cloaks on the road.
passages.original: Πορευομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ὑπεστρώννυον τὰ ἱμάτια ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ

passages.text: And as He approached the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples began to praise God joyfully in a loud voice for all the miracles they had seen: “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus approached the descent from the Mount of Olives.
A large crowd of His disciples followed Him.
The disciples felt great joy.
They began to praise God.
They spoke with loud voices.
They praised God for all the miracles they had seen.
They said, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!”
They also said, “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
passages.original: ἐγγίζοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤδη πρὸς τῇ καταβάσει τοῦ ὄρους τῶν Ἐλαιῶν ἤρξαντο ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν χαίροντες αἰνεῖν τὸν Θεὸν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ περὶ πασῶν ὧν εἶδον δυνάμεων λέγοντες Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ὁ Βασιλεὺς ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου Ἐν οὐρανῷ εἰρήνη καὶ δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις

passages.text: But some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!”
passages.sermon:
Some Pharisees stood in the crowd.
These Pharisees spoke to Jesus.
They called Jesus “Teacher.”
They told Jesus to rebuke His disciples.
passages.original: Καί τινες τῶν Φαρισαίων ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν Διδάσκαλε ἐπιτίμησον τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου

passages.text: “I tell you,” He answered, “if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
He answered them directly.
He said, “I tell you this truth.
If these disciples remain silent,
The stones themselves will cry out.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν οὗτοι σιωπήσουσιν οἱ λίθοι κράξουσιν

passages.text: As Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it and said, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
passages.sermon:
Jesus approached Jerusalem.
He saw the city.
He wept over the city.
He spoke to the city.
He said, “If you had known today what would bring you peace, it would be good for you.
But now these things are hidden from your eyes.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὡς ἤγγισεν ἰδὼν τὴν πόλιν ἔκλαυσεν ἐπ’ αὐτήν λέγων ὅτι Εἰ ἔγνως ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ καὶ σὺ τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην νῦν δὲ ἐκρύβη ἀπὸ ὀφθαλμῶν σου

passages.text: For the days will come upon you when your enemies will barricade you and surround you and hem you in on every side.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Jerusalem.
He warned the city.
He said that difficult days would come.
Enemies would come against Jerusalem.
They would build barricades around the city.
They would surround Jerusalem.
They would trap the people from every side.
passages.original: ὅτι ἥξουσιν ἡμέραι ἐπὶ σὲ καὶ παρεμβαλοῦσιν οἱ ἐχθροί σου χάρακά σοι καὶ περικυκλώσουσίν σε καὶ συνέξουσίν σε πάντοθεν

passages.text: They will level you to the ground—you and the children within your walls. They will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation from God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Jerusalem.
He warned the city.
Enemies will destroy you.
They will destroy your children inside you.
They will tear you down to the ground.
They will not leave one stone on another in you.
This will happen because you did not recognize the time when God visited you.
passages.original: καὶ ἐδαφιοῦσίν σε καὶ τὰ τέκνα σου ἐν σοί καὶ οὐκ ἀφήσουσιν λίθον ἐπὶ λίθον ἐν σοί ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἔγνως τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς σου

passages.text: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there.
passages.sermon: Jesus entered the temple courts.\r\nHe saw people selling things there.\r\nJesus began to drive out those who were selling.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας

passages.text: He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people in the temple.\r\nHe said, “It is written: My house will be a house of prayer.”\r\nHe said, “You have made it a den of robbers.”
passages.original: λέγων αὐτοῖς Γέγραπται Καὶ ἔσται ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ἐποιήσατε Σπήλαιον λῃστῶν

passages.text: Jesus was teaching at the temple every day, but the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people were intent on killing Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught every day in the temple.
The chief priests wanted to kill Jesus.
The scribes wanted to kill Jesus.
The leaders of the people wanted to kill Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦν διδάσκων τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἀπολέσαι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τοῦ λαοῦ

passages.text: Yet they could not find a way to do so, because all the people hung on His words.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests, scribes, and leaders wanted to kill Jesus.
They could not find a way to do it.
All the people listened closely to Jesus.
The people paid careful attention to His words.
passages.original: καὶ οὐχ εὕρισκον τὸ τί ποιήσωσιν ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἅπας ἐξεκρέματο αὐτοῦ ἀκούων
